verdict.justification: Both deliverables accurately extract the 41 prepaid expense invoices and 25 insurance invoices, apply the correct 6-month and 12-month amortization rules, properly recognize the BCBS one-month prepayment lag, and reconcile to the General Ledger balances. However, Deliverable B is much better structured and more useful from an accounting perspective. On the Prepaid Summary tab, Deliverable B includes a 'YTD Amortization Expense by GL Account (Jan - Apr 2025)' table (rows 33-43) that summarizes the monthly journal entry debits by specific COA expense account (e.g., 5720, 6020, 6760, 6762, 7001, 5015, 5400) and credits to 1250/1251, whereas Deliverable A only maps the expense account numbers at the individual invoice level without summarizing them on the summary tab. Additionally, on the detailed schedule tabs, Deliverable B includes both the Expense GL # and the Expense Account Name (e.g., '6760' and 'IT Services/Agreements'), while Deliverable A only lists the account number. Deliverable B also avoids cluttering the detailed schedules with redundant single-row vendor subtotals for vendors with only one invoice (like ALTAIR, AMESITE, and CIMSOURCE in Deliverable A) and extends the schedule through the projected run-off of existing invoices.

decisive_issues.issue: Includes redundant subtotal rows for single-invoice vendors on the detail schedule, adding unnecessary clutter.
Omits Expense Account names on the detailed schedule and lacks a summary of amortization expense by GL expense account on the Summary tab.
